alertsLaPorteCounty.description:
Lingering low level moisture and light winds have been favorable
for fog formation across the region early this morning.
Visibilities will be highly variable due to the patchy nature of
the fog, but at least localized visibilities of one quarter of a
mile or less are expected through 9 AM EST. The fog is expected
to dissipate after 930 AM EST. Motorists should be prepared for
rapid changes in visibilities across short distances.

nearbyCountiesFullText.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 16 at 1:37AM CST by NWS Chicago IL
nearbyCountiesFullText.description:
Areas of fog are expected to continue through daybreak across
northwest Indiana. Visibilities may vary rapidly over short
distances with localized visibilities as low as one quarter mile
at times. With temperatures near freezing, slick spots may develop
on untreated elevated surfaces. The fog is expected to slowly
lift and dissipate after sunrise this morning.

discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 160755
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
255 AM EST Mon Nov 16 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Patchy fog early this morning. The fog may be locally dense.
  Visibilities are expected to improve after 9 AM EST.

- A moderating temperature trend this week. The warmest days are 
  Thursday through Saturday with highs in the low to mid 60s.

- Mainly dry conditions are expected this week with some rain
  chances returning by next weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 250 AM EST Mon Nov 16 2026

In the near term, patchy fog concerns will be the primary forecast 
issue to deal with. Visibilities early this morning are showing a 
wide range across the region, with lowest vsbys in spots that had a 
more delayed scattering of low cloud cover yesterday afternoon where 
crossover temps were a bit higher. Near term forecast soundings do 
depict some favorable vertical moisture lapse rates for at least 
shallow fog formation this morning and will continue this mention 
through 14Z. Some sporadic one quarter mile visibilities have been 
noted this morning, but especially in favored locations susceptible 
to fog and these lower vsbys. Will continue to monitor trends 
this morning to determine if a more focused Dense Fog Advisory 
will be needed. 

The longwave pattern will finally begin to show some progression 
beginning later today, but this will be a slow process through 
Wednesday as longwave pattern will likely show some resilience 
to change this week with preference to a central CONUS
background longwave ridge. Some low clouds linger across far 
northwest Ohio this morning, but these should begin to diminish 
or shift eastward today as low level winds become more westerly.
Skies should be mostly sunny today with a potential of some low
coverage low clouds mid-late morning with mixing out of shallow
moisture/fog early this morning. Otherwise, a weak mid level 
short wave trough topping the central CONUS ridge into the 
Great Lakes may be enough combined with weak mid level warm 
advection for some patchy high clouds across the southern Great 
Lakes late this afternoon into this evening. With moderation of 
low level airmass and onset of weak low level warm advection 
today, highs in the lower 50s still appear reasonable.

Some better progression in upper pattern is noted late Tuesday 
into Wednesday as an upper level trough approaching the west 
coast today ejects into the northern Plains Wednesday night and 
into southeast Ontario Thursday night. Moisture transport in 
advance of this disturbance still looks to largely 
circumnavigate the local area into Wednesday night as persistent
Mid Atlantic low level anticyclone cuts off Gulf moisture 
transport. Axis of some pre-frontal moisture pooling will 
become weak and elongated in west-east sense across the southern
Great Lakes late Wednesday night into Thursday as the upper 
level short wave has some difficulty in lowering heights with 
much southward extent due to stable nature of wave pattern and 
stubborn breakdown of longwave ridge. PoPs below mentionable 
levels still look appropriate for Thursday/Thursday night with 
perhaps a few sprinkles across western Great Lakes late 
Thursday coincident with the weak elevated moisture axis and
along southern fringe of better short wave trough forcing. A 
transition back to much above normal temperatures is in store 
for Thursday and Friday as expansive homogeneous "warm sector" 
overspreads Ohio Valley and southern Great Lakes.

Induced upper level short wave ridging will build in behind the 
departing northern Great Lakes wave for Friday, while a larger 
scale upper trough digs shifts across the northern Rockies on 
Friday. Overall pattern we have witnessed recently and progged 
to continue in medium range guidance is for lack of 
consolidation/phasing of several negative upper height 
perturbations and a very disjointed nature to wave pattern. As 
a result, stronger upstream frontal convergence with this short 
wave for Saturday looks to wane somewhat with eastward extent as
the trough approaches the western Great Lakes. The transition 
to more progression with these short wave by end of work week 
leaves duration of better low level moisture transport more 
limited with northward extent with better moisture quality 
confined to the central/southern Plains. Nonetheless, would 
expect a somewhat more impressive narrow pooled moisture axis to
work into the area Saturday and Saturday night with better 
chance of some isoalted-scattered frontally induced showers. 
Highs will remain well above normal Saturday in advance of this
wave cooling back to the mid 50s for second half of the 
weekend.

The frontal boundary from weekend system will probably hang up 
across the local area to begin next week as medium range guidance 
depicts a generally low amplitude flow setup. This should
support temps at or slightly below normal to begin the week. 
Possibility of lingering baroclinic zone across the region and 
additional eastern Pacific waves in this more suppressed low 
amplitude pattern could be favorable for additional short 
waves/weak to modest advective forcing episodes that would 
support some precip chances next week. However, this appears 
more likely beyond this forecast valid period and is of very low
confidence at this time.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z TUESDAY/...
Issued at 1248 AM EST Mon Nov 16 2026

VFR/MVFR conditions this evening will potentially deteriorate 
to IFR toward 10-13z. Several sites around the area are already
dropping to around 1-3SM, with a few fluctuating to below 1SM 
(typical spots for lower visibility). Uncertainty exists with 
regards to the extent of the FG/BR-it could be fairly shallow. 
Guidance keeps visibility MVFR except briefly during the 10-13z
time frame, so have a tempo for IFR VIS in that period. It's 
possible we see LIFR ceilings/vis, but confidence wasn't high 
enough to include at this point.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Marsili
AVIATION...MCD

spc.text:
SPC AC 160527

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1127 PM CST Sun Nov 15 2026

   Valid 161200Z - 171200Z

   ...NO THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Precipitation across parts of the Pacific Coast into Great Basin may
   be accompanied by some risk for lightning today through tonight, but
   this potential is expected to remain low, with any such activity
   short-lived and sparse in coverage.

   ...Discussion...
   Latest model output continues to indicate splitting mid-level flow
   across the eastern Pacific into the Pacific Coast during this
   period, in response to upstream amplification within the westerlies,
   which is likely to include a vigorous short wave trough digging
   across the northeastern mid-latitude Pacific later today through
   tonight.  As this occurs, consolidating preceding troughing is
   forecast to dig toward the California coast, before pivoting inland,
   to the south of building mid-level ridging across British Columbia. 

   Farther east, it appears that a more prominent positively tilted
   ridge may build to the east of the southern Rockies through Upper
   Midwest by late tonight, within a broader area of higher mean
   heights slowly shifting eastward across the interior United States. 
   Downstream, flow is likely to remain sharply confluent into
   increasingly sheared mid-level troughing shifting away from the
   northern Atlantic Seaboard, but lingering across much of the
   Southeast and eastern Gulf Basin.  

   Beneath this regime, guidance indicates that expansive cold surface
   ridging will be maintained, centered across the Ohio Valley into
   southern Mid Atlantic and an influence across most areas east of the
   Rockies, with the exception of the northern high plains, where
   surface troughing will begin to deepen ahead of a cold front
   advancing into and through the intermountain west.

   ...Pacific Coast into Great Basin...
   It appears that the primary mid-level thermal trough, including 500
   mb temperatures around -25 to -30 C, may not spread much inland of
   western Washington, Oregon and northern California coastal areas
   prior to sunset this evening, with associated destabilization
   generally forecast to remain quite weak throughout the post-frontal
   regime.  Based on forecast soundings, the evolution of thermodynamic
   profiles conducive to short-lived stronger convection capable of
   producing lightning does not appear out of the question.  However,
   any such activity seems likely to remain too transient and sparse in
   coverage to justify 10 percent thunderstorm probabilities.

   Meanwhile, ahead of the cold front, sufficient moistening and
   steepening of lapse rates with mid-level forcing for ascent may
   occur to contribute to increasing convection across parts of
   southern/eastern Nevada into western Utah and northwestern Arizona
   by late tonight.  However, similar to the post-frontal environment,
   destabilization is forecast to remain quite weak, and it remains
   unclear whether thermodynamic profiles will support more than widely
   spaced short-lived weak thunderstorms.

   ..Kerr/Chalmers.. 11/16/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 160651

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1251 AM CST Mon Nov 16 2026

   Valid 171200Z - 181200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are unlikely Tuesday.

   ...Southwest...
   A shortwave trough, initially over northern Baja will rapidly lift
   northeastward across the Desert Southwest and into the Rockies
   Tuesday. The overall upper-air pattern is forecast to amplify with
   the trough deepening and downstream ridging over the central US also
   intensifying. Ascent and height falls from the upper trough will
   intensify a surface low and trailing cold front across the northern
   Great Basin and into western WY. This will support an increase in
   southerly low-level flow over much of the Plains and Southwest,
   though available moisture will remain quite limited owing to the
   prior Gulf frontal intrusion. Still, a modest increase in moisture
   and instability will likely support thunderstorms across parts of
   AZ/UT and southern NV into western WY/CO/NM. Moderate to strong
   deep-layer flow will accompany this shortwave trough, but the
   limited thermodynamic profiles will largely negate organized-severe
   potential. Small hail and locally gusty winds may occur with the
   strongest storms across parts of the Southwest where buoyancy is
   forecast to be the largest.

   ...West Coast...
   A second upper low will approach the northern CA ad OR coasts late
   Tuesday. Strong height falls and cold mid-level temperature (-20 to
   -25 C) may support a band of shallow convection along the cold
   front, possibly accompanied by sporadic lightning flashes.
   Upper-level wind fields will be strong, but scant inland
   surface-based instability is expected to limit severe potential.

   ...FL...
   East of the Rockies, an expansive surface ridge over the
   central/eastern CONUS will continue to limit moisture return and
   thunderstorm potential. The exception is across parts of the FL
   Peninsula and Keys, ahead of a weak mid/upper-level trough.
   Scattered showers and thunderstorms ongoing over the Gulf may
   eventually move inland over parts of the southern Peninsula where
   modest buoyancy will be in place. Additional storms are possible on
   the Atlantic coast where onshore flow may allow for weak
   destabilization. Poor mid-level lapse rates and overall buoyancy
   suggest severe storms are unlikely.

   ..Lyons.. 11/16/2026

spc.text:
SPC AC 160827

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0227 AM CST Mon Nov 16 2026

   Valid 181200Z - 191200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are not expected Wednesday.

   ...Synopsis...
   The shortwave trough over the Rockies early Wednesday is forecast to
   eject eastward across the Plains to the western Great Lakes as the
   second western US trough moves into the Great Basin. High pressure
   will persist over the eastern US, as southwesterly flow aloft
   strengthens over the West. Onshore flow over the West Coast beneath
   the second upper trough may support a shallow convective band with
   sporadic lightning flashes. Additional storms are possible with a
   weak upper low over southern FL. Instability is forecast to be very
   weak and severe storms are unlikely.

   ...Central Plains...
   The surface low, attendant to the first upper trough, will move
   northeastward toward the Canadian border dragging a fairly strong
   cold front across the northern/central Rockies and Plains. The
   strong surface pressure gradient will bolster southerly winds and
   initiate modest moisture return Wednesday afternoon. However,
   surface dewpoints are only expected to reach the lower to middle 40s
   F ahead of the cold front. This will severely limit available
   buoyancy with most model guidance showing MUCAPE of 200-400 J/kg.
   Still, isolated low-topped Thunderstorms are possible given the
   strong frontal forcing and steeper low-level lapse rates. Severe
   storms are not expected.

   ..Lyons.. 11/16/2026
